 Campaign spending surges in race for California's 13th Congressional District 
 Political campaigns are continuing to invest heavily in advertising and voter outreach as Election Day approaches. By Jason Oliveira Thursday, October 29, 2026 12:29AM Share Follow ABC30 on Google FRESNO, Calif. (KFSN) -- Money continues to flow into 13th Congressional District race as midterm elections approach
 As the midterm elections approach, money continues to pour into some of Central California's most closely watched congressional races, including the race in the 13th Congressional District.
 The 13th District contest remains among the congressional races drawing significant attention in Central California as candidates and campaigns continue to attract funding ahead of the elections.
 With the midterm elections nearing, the flow of money into the region's high-profile congressional contests, including the 13th District race, continues.
 As Election Day approaches, campaign funding continues to play a major role in the closely watched race for California's 13th Congressional District, with both parties investing heavily in a contest viewed as highly competitive.
 Political campaigns are spending heavily on advertising and outreach in the final stretch of the campaign. With one week remaining before the election, the 13th Congressional District race has attracted significant attention, fueled in part by major donor contributions.
 "There has been a fair amount of spending going on in that district. I think part of it is republicans have a plethora of money to spend and democrats are probably wisely not taking anything for granted," said Fresno State political science professor and political analyst Dr. Thomas Holyoke.
 In the high-stakes contest, Democratic incumbent Adam Gray holds a significant fundraising advantage. Gray's campaign brought in more than $5 million, compared with $2.89 million raised by former Stockton Mayor Kevin Lincoln.
 Gray also holds nearly double the cash on hand, with $1.2 million available to spend compared with Lincoln's $682,000.

 Holyoke said the amount of money being spent during this election cycle is unprecedented.
 "This year we have exceeded two years ago and two years ago was a presidential election year. We're actually spending more money this time than last time and we're talking in the billions of dollars," Holyoke said.
 While both campaigns received their largest share of contributions from California, out-of-state donations have also played a significant role.
 Gray received $278,000 from New York and $224,000 from Massachusetts. Lincoln received $278,000 from Texas and nearly $225,000 from Florida as he seeks to compete in the Democratic-leaning district.
 "The House of Representatives is up for grabs so any district that can anyway be competitive anywhere in the nation is something that is a big deal to the people who run both the republican and democratic parties," Holyoke said.
 As the final days of the campaign unfold, both candidates are expected to rely on their financial resources to compete for voters' attention across the Central Valley through television, digital advertising and other outreach efforts.
